action: No action needed; for awareness. Candidates should use only the official Inep and gov.br addresses and ignore messages asking for data or payment about Enem results.
exec: Brazil's national exam body says its website is being attacked; no impact reported, but exam-result phishing is a likely follow-on.
impact: None confirmed; the minister said the attacks are under control. The nature of the attacks and whether any succeeded were not stated.
org: Inep (Instituto Nacional de Estudos e Pesquisas Educacionais)
plain: Brazil's education minister said hackers have been attacking the Inep website during the second day of the Enem national exam, and that the attacks are under control.

key_findings: Minister of Education Leonardo Barchini said on 15 November 2026 that the Inep website has been suffering hacker attacks.
He spoke during Vice President Geraldo Alckmin's visit to Inep, on the second day of Enem 2026.
He said the attacks are being controlled; he gave no counts, origin or technique.
Press reports say it is unclear whether any attack succeeded; the ministry did not answer requests for details.

summary: Brazil's Education Minister Leonardo Barchini said on 15 November, during the second day of the Enem exam, that the Inep website has been the target of hacker attacks and that they are under control. He gave no numbers, source or method, and press reports say it is unclear whether any attack succeeded. The statement is the only account; no technical report has been published.
title: Brazil's education minister says Inep website under hacker attack during Enem

validation.note: Two Brazilian outlets report the same ministerial statement; no technical detail published.

review.note: Compared with Gazeta do Povo and Diario de Pernambuco: 15 Nov, minister Barchini, day 2 of Enem, under control, no details, success unclear; severity 1.
